title: Video streaming
summary: Transcoding pipelines, adaptive bitrate and CDN economics.
prompt: Design a video platform: creators upload videos, which are processed for playback on phones, laptops and TVs; viewers watch on demand with quick start and little buffering.

requirements: Functional: upload, transcode, publish, watch with adaptive quality, resume position, view counts.
Non-functional: playback starts in ~2 s and rarely stalls; global audience; storage and egress cost matter a lot.
estimation: 100M hours watched a day at ~3 Mbit/s: 100M × 3,600 s × 3 Mbit ÷ 86,400 s ≈ 12.5 Tbit/s average egress.
500 hours uploaded per minute; a ladder of ~6 renditions roughly doubles to triples source storage.
Egress dominates cost, so cache hit rate at the edge is the key lever.
api: POST /uploads → resumable upload session; POST /videos {uploadId, title} → {videoId, status}.
GET /videos/{id}/manifest → an HLS or DASH manifest listing renditions and segment URLs on the CDN.
POST /videos/{id}/progress {position} for resume; view events go to analytics.
data: videos(id, owner, title, status, duration, renditions) metadata.
Object storage: source files, and segments per rendition (2–6 s chunks) under immutable paths.
View events stream into an aggregation pipeline, not a per-view database write.
design: Upload to object storage; a pipeline splits the source into chunks and transcodes them in parallel into a ladder (e.g. 240p–4K) and codecs.
Publish writes manifests; the CDN caches segments close to viewers, pulling from an origin shield in front of storage.
The player measures throughput and buffer level and switches renditions between segments (adaptive bitrate).
deepDives: Parallel transcoding: chunk-level jobs make a long video finish in minutes; a DAG of tasks handles thumbnails, captions and checks.
Start-up time: start with a low rendition, keep the first segments short, and prefetch the manifest.
Long tail: most views go to a small share of videos; popular content sits in edge caches while rarely watched videos may only exist at origin, or in fewer renditions.
bottlenecks: Transcoding cost: transcode popular videos into more renditions and codecs; give long-tail uploads a basic ladder first.
Origin overload on a viral video: an origin shield collapses many edge misses into one fetch.
View counting at scale: aggregate events in streams; show approximate counts live.
tradeoffs: More renditions = smoother playback but more storage and transcode compute.
Newer codecs cut bandwidth substantially but cost more CPU to encode and are not supported on every device.
Own CDN vs commercial CDN: control and unit cost vs time to market and global reach.

rubric.text: Estimated egress bandwidth and identified it as the main cost.
Designed a parallel transcoding pipeline into a bitrate ladder.
Explained segmented streaming with manifests and adaptive bitrate.
Used a CDN with an origin shield.
Handled resumable uploads and processing status.
Aggregated view events instead of writing per view.
Treated popular and long-tail content differently.
Weighed codec, rendition and CDN cost trade-offs.
